data.title: bn-6zcm: Qualify authenticated host process collector for cold trials

data.body: [HIGH][CWE-862][CWE-345] A matching previous_response_id authorizes an arbitrary replacement prompt instead of binding continuation history. The first request alone is checked against ContextExpectation at lines 962-980; after a no-tool terminal, this branch accepts any input when the caller repeats the last response ID. Against the target code, an exact offline witness returned first=200, second=200 and valid=true for prepared task followed by INJECTED replacement prompt; the checked-in test at test-native-codex-boundary.py:1467-1484 explicitly blesses a changed second instruction. An admitted untrusted worker can therefore spend the host provider credential on arbitrary model input after one assigned request while the relay receipt claims valid context binding. Retained v29 did not exercise this path: its four requests omit previous_response_id and use exact append-only tool history, so this is a latent live-boundary defect rather than evidence that v29 was abused. Reject every request after a no-tool terminal for one Codex execution, or bind the response ID to the exact prior accepted input and authorized append-only continuation. risk:high checklist: (1) failure modes are arbitrary prompt/history injection, provider-credit abuse, and a falsely valid relay receipt; (2) validate changed instructions/input, stale/cross-run/null IDs, post-terminal concurrency, and exact allowed continuation bytes; (3) rollback by disabling response-ID continuation and terminating/quarantining affected relay sessions; (4) monitor and alert on any previous_response_id request, especially after zero tool calls, and on context-digest changes; (5) validate an exact host-authorized continuation transcript, not possession of an opaque response ID alone.

[MEDIUM][CWE-754] Relay finalization reports settled and valid while the last upstream terminal still contains unresolved tool calls. Lines 1117-1123 retain pending_tool_calls and pending_tool_items, but reconciliation here checks only request/attempt/terminal counts and completed terminals, and finalize at lines 1341-1354 never requires both pending collections to be empty. An offline target-code witness completed one response containing exec_command, sent no function_call_output, then produced valid=true, reasons=[], tool_call_count=1. The native qualifier trusts relay_receipt[valid] at qualify-skeleton-process-monitor-native.py:664 without independently requiring a zero-call final terminal. V29 itself ended [1,1,1,0], so its chain completed. Make finalize add an unresolved-tool-call-chain reason unless both pending collections are empty, require a zero-call final terminal in the outer qualifier, and add crash/clean-exit regressions after each tool terminal.

[MEDIUM][CWE-345] Final FD exec launders an earlier pinned executable and side effects into an Investigation role. This branch rejects only earlier /proc execs; it permits a pinned /bin/sh prefix, then returns the final /proc/self/fd role. Later approval at lines 3013-3053 uses only that final role. A focused target-code witness with exec_chain=[/bin/sh,/proc/self/fd/9] and a pre-final write(3,forged) was accepted with role=investigation and lost_events=0. This violates the documented exact FD-child attribution and can let non-Investigation behavior mutate trial state before its stdout is retained as an Investigation original. Require an FD child to have exactly one successful exec, or explicitly prove and reject every pre-final epoch and side effect; add adversarial prefix-exec, nonstdout-write, and state-mutation regressions.

[MEDIUM][CWE-362][CWE-345] The trace parser keys process identity only by numeric PID, so sequential PID lifetimes collapse into one approved child. Parent, execs, exits, writes, and topology are merged in the same Process; normal pinned children do not require a start-tick snapshot. A target-code witness reused PID 301 for two sequential exact Teapot children and still settled with lost_events=0, one Teapot execution row whose exec_chain length was 2, and only second newline retained as stdout. On PID-namespace wrap or reuse this loses one execution and its first output while claiming complete accounting. Key process state by PID plus lifetime/start identity, reject a second clone/exit lifetime for an existing PID unless a new authenticated start tick is present, and bind all executions and stdout to that lifetime. Add a forced-reuse parser regression.

[MEDIUM][CWE-754][CWE-223] Caught and nonfatal signal records are silently ignored. Only terminal killed-by lines set Process.signal; a normal strace line such as --- SIGUSR1 {...} --- falls through without a parse failure. Injecting that exact record into an otherwise valid target trace produced accepted=true, lost_events=0, signal=None, parse_failures=[], contrary to skeleton-process-monitor.md:9-14, which says signals fail the attempt. A signal can alter control flow while the collector certifies an unsignalled complete tree. Parse every strace signal-delivery record, retain it, and reject any signal in an assessed tree unless a narrowly enumerated infrastructure contract proves it; add caught, ignored, thread-directed, and resumed-syscall signal regressions.

[MEDIUM][CWE-284][CWE-732] The independent Podman validator certifies arbitrary writable bind mounts. fields.get(ro, true) treats omitted ro as read-only although Podman defaults a bind to writable; the code accepts arbitrary absolute sources/destinations and does not enforce the expected /workspace, /runtime, /gateway and pinned-binary destination set or protected-root exclusions. After rebinding the argv digest, target-code witnesses accepted /etc to /workspace and /home/bob/.ssh to /stolen without ro, and also accepted a writable source shadowing /opt/scourge-bin/scourge. The current native boundary builder supplies safer canonical mounts, so retained v29 is not shown to use an unsafe argv, but the collector documentation explicitly promises rejection even for an unsafe pre-bound configuration. Require an exact mount manifest with destination-specific access, canonical source identity, overlap/protected-root checks, and explicit ro=true everywhere except the two enumerated writable roots; regression-test shadowing and credential-root mounts.

[MEDIUM][CWE-345][CWE-706] Native qualification marks non-resolving artifact references valid because it checks only count and a string prefix. _artifact_ref emits bn-6zcm-native/retained/artifacts/NAME, while this driver writes NAME directly under bn-6zcm-native-qualification-v29.json.artifacts/retained/. Independent verification found 75 references, zero signed paths resolvable under the v29 artifact root, and 75 digest-matching files only after manually discarding the signed directory prefix. The production Evidence reader resolves every evidence-root-relative component and hashes it, so these references are not consumable. Generate a fresh receipt with files staged at the exact referenced paths, then resolve and rehash every call/child reference through the production reader before valid can become true; bind envelope and events as references through the same seam.

[MEDIUM][CWE-223] The final receipt hard-codes rejected_attempts only through v24 and omits the preserved v28 rejection that directly motivated the final write-order rule. Evidence inventory confirms v25 accepted, v26 partial preflight, v27 accepted, v28 rejected, and v29 accepted; the retained v28 raw trace is 43,292,620 bytes with SHA-256 3a9ee9465ac7c21e7256d44aa12bc3bef3d365e8bfaaae76b1dfcb46eade8153, yet v29 reports only v1-v24. The rows also assert private_evidence_preserved without durable artifact references or manifests, so planned cleanup of older /tmp roots can make that assertion unverifiable. This is security-relevant first-attempt amnesia: a receipt claiming final qualification omits the last fail-closed run and cannot reconstruct the evidence lineage. Replace the handwritten list with a complete ordered attempt_history through the accepted run, including disposition, failure reason, source/driver revision, durable artifact-root reference and manifest, whether tracing started, and teardown state; migrate evidence needed for the claim before cleanup.

[MEDIUM][CWE-345] The native receipt is not bound to the harness and key that produced its valid decision. assignment_sha256 covers only bone, image, command and staged binary pins; it omits this qualifier, responses_relay.py, native_codex_boundary.py, the compatibility driver, the target Git tree, and the monitor-key digest. The HMAC is self-verified with monitor.key stored beside the trace, and receipt construction at lines 678-923 publishes no producer manifest or independent key commitment. Thus a stale or locally modified qualifier can weaken valid, relay, fixture or provenance checks, issue an internally consistent receipt/key/envelope, then source can be restored; the receipt cannot prove it came from target 82ad12a. Concretely v29 observed at 16:30:01Z, before the target commit at 16:36:40Z, and current source hashes exist only in later narration, not the receipt. Bind a complete control-source manifest and exact target tree plus SHA-256 of the precommitted monitor key into the assignment before launch; publish and independently recompute that manifest, and recapture only after freezing the target.

data.reason: BLOCK at exact target 82ad12a21352b4b8ea363f389577361e94247c2f over base 8a531990fb206a984e65458c86321776ca69a54f (full binary diff SHA-256 9feae3d43de8fc974820f980570234853e62552898cffa0c2be94c4c7fb6bb51). Nine open findings: HIGH th-vb8oev allows arbitrary provider-backed follow-up prompts by presenting the last response ID; MEDIUM th-2btlm5 settles unresolved tool calls, th-3tghod launders pre-FD exec behavior into Investigation, th-kj8dcy collapses PID lifetimes, th-2flq8x ignores caught signals, th-2c9ohv accepts arbitrary writable binds, th-1s4syj validates 75 non-resolving artifact refs by prefix only, th-3ao2ne omits the preserved v28 rejection/history, and th-1e8uzm does not bind the receipt to its producing harness, target tree, or independent monitor-key commitment. V29 receipt/envelope/events/raw/snapshot hashes and HMAC were independently consistent, but that does not close the path/provenance failures. Fresh offline witnesses reproduced all code-path false acceptances; 29 collector tests and the focused response-ID test pass because current tests omit or bless these cases. No provider/model network or auth-file access was used.

data.body: [MEDIUM][CWE-345][CWE-20] Relay finality trusts only the terminal response.output and never requires individual output items to be completed. _response_tool_chain at lines 292-322 accepts function_call and custom_tool_call items regardless of item status; _terminal_receipt here validates only the top-level response status and, for SSE, ignores prior response.output_item.done events. Exact offline witnesses accepted an in_progress function call followed by its output and then an empty terminal, accepted a one-shot in_progress message as a zero-tool terminal, and forwarded a completed exec_command output-item event followed by terminal output=[]; each finalized settled=true, valid=true, reasons=[], with the SSE case recording tool_call_count=0. An inconsistent or adversarial upstream can therefore cause client-visible tool activity or incomplete output while the relay certifies a complete zero-tool boundary. Require completed status and required fields on every item, reconcile the ordered SSE item stream byte-for-byte with terminal output, and fail closed on omission, mutation, duplication, or incomplete items.

[MEDIUM][CWE-345] The receipt asserts that the staged Scourge binary was built from ca4019d/tree 419ade without any source-to-binary derivation. stage_exact accepts a caller-supplied path and caller-supplied digest, then lines 712-723 discard the source path and attach the producer Git commit/tree and profile=debug. No isolated build command, build log, locked dependency/toolchain identity, product-source manifest, or independent build attestation is captured or bound into the assignment. V32 proves only that executed bytes hash to 5dcfc959...7499. A matching target/debug/build artifact has an 09:03 timestamp while ca4019d was committed at 12:53, demonstrating that these bytes predate the claimed source revision; current target/debug/scourge is different. A caller can therefore relabel arbitrary pinned bytes as a clean current-source build while all receipt checks pass. Build in a fresh verified export with locked inputs, retain the command/log/toolchain/lock and binary digest in the producer manifest and assignment, then recapture native evidence.
